Write the mean function as $\mu$, not as $f$.
The mean function is the population mean of the outcome given the inputs, $\mu(x)$.
In a group that uses shared macros (see [Using shared macros](#using-shared-macros)),
write it `\truemeanf{x}`.

Name the object you mean.
When the text refers to the prediction function as a concept,
the rule that turns an input into a predicted outcome,
write the prediction function, not the fitted mean function.
Write it `\predfnf{x}` (symbol $g$), or `\epredfnf{x}` for an estimated one.
Use the fitted or estimated mean function only where the text is about
estimating the mean function $\mu$ itself.

::: {#exm-mean-vs-prediction-function}

## Mean function and prediction function

> ❌ The expected squared error of the fitted mean function at $x$ is $\E{(y - \hat{f}(x))^2}$.
>
> ✅ The expected squared error of the estimated prediction function at $x$ is $\E{(y - \hat{g}(x))^2}$,
> and its bias is $\E{\hat{g}(x)} - \mu(x)$.

The ✅ version names the prediction function where the concept is a prediction,
and keeps $\mu$ for the mean it is compared with.

:::
